definition: Institutional, governmental, supranational or corporate sources used as evidence for policy frameworks, statistics, programme reports, international comparisons or educational governance contexts.
representative_cited_authors: OECD (236); American Psychological Association (92); UNESCO (59); European Commission (31); M. O. Martin (30)
interpretive_use: Signals papers that position EJPE findings in relation to policy agendas, large-scale evidence, official definitions or institutional monitoring rather than primarily to a named psychological theory.

lineage_label: Developmental, family, peer and ecological traditions
definition: Developmental, ecological and social-developmental traditions concerned with family processes, peer relations, adolescence, bullying, adjustment, identity, socialisation and development in nested contexts.
representative_cited_authors: U. Bronfenbrenner (80); R. C. Pianta (65); J. Nurmi (63); K. R. Wentzel (63); D. A. Kenny (62); R. W. Roeser (54); S. G. West (52); N. Kiuru (51)
interpretive_use: Helps identify work that treats educational outcomes as embedded in family, peer, school and wider developmental ecologies.

definition: Didactic and classroom-practice sources concerned with curriculum knowledge, instruction, teacher practices, disciplinary learning and the organisation of teaching and learning activities.
representative_cited_authors: J. Hattie (115); L. Verschaffel (75); M. Kunter (74); Y. Li (60); F. Marton (59); M. Brunner (57); P. A. Alexander (55); R. Glaser (55)
interpretive_use: Marks papers that connect psychological analysis to concrete instructional practices and classroom knowledge traditions.

lineage_label: Educational policy, sociology and comparative education
definition: Sociological, comparative and policy-oriented traditions addressing educational systems, inequality, reform, institutional arrangements, social class, culture and cross-national comparison.
representative_cited_authors: J. Baumert (115); A. Kaplan (64); A. S. Bryk (40); H. Cooper (40); Z. Wen (27)
interpretive_use: Shows when EJPE articles anchor psychological questions in broader institutional, sociological or comparative accounts of education.

definition: Cognitive and individual-difference sources focused on achievement, ability, intelligence, memory, learning processes, reading, problem solving, academic performance and cognitive development.
representative_cited_authors: W. Schneider (97); W. Kintsch (69); M. Pressley (61); M. T. H. Chi (61); Y. Liu (60); B. Spinath (59); G. Schraw (55); J. S. Hyde (53)
interpretive_use: Indicates work in which educational phenomena are interpreted through cognitive mechanisms, learner characteristics and achievement-related constructs.

definition: Constructivist, social-cognitive and interactionist traditions linking knowledge construction, conflict, coordination of perspectives, peer interaction and social mediation of cognitive development.
representative_cited_authors: J. Piaget (131); G. Mugny (94); A.-N. Perret-Clermont (87); A. L. Brown (83); R. S. Siegler (75); W. Doise (75); J. H. Flavell (74); L. Mason (43)
interpretive_use: This lineage is especially relevant to EJPE's founding concern with educational interaction as a source of psychological development.

definition: Sources on designed interventions, instructional programmes, pedagogical design, feedback, scaffolding, assessment for learning and experimentally evaluated educational supports.
representative_cited_authors: R. E. Mayer (89); J. Sweller (64); X. Wang (60); P. A. Kirschner (47); J. Liu (43); F. Paas (41); H. Li (40); R. E. Slavin (36)
interpretive_use: Highlights papers where citation ancestry is tied to improving or testing educational designs and instructional tools.

definition: Motivational, self-regulatory and identity traditions addressing goals, interest, engagement, self-efficacy, attribution, emotions, agency, persistence and learner identity.
representative_cited_authors: J. S. Eccles (248); R. M. Ryan (212); E. L. Deci (207); H. W. Marsh (203); A. Bandura (196); A. Wigfield (193); P. R. Pintrich (186); R. Pekrun (171)
interpretive_use: Shows the growth of later international educational-psychology traditions around engagement, motivation and self-regulated learning.

definition: Methodological, psychometric and statistical sources used for measurement models, scale development, latent-variable analysis, reliability, validity, multilevel modelling and quantitative inference.
representative_cited_authors: P. M. Bentler (193); J. Cohen (158); O. Ludtke (135); L. Hu (100); O. Koller (89); B. O. Muthen (83); A. F. Hayes (72); J. Wang (71)
interpretive_use: Marks papers whose intellectual ancestry is methodological or measurement-oriented, often supporting empirical modelling rather than substantive theory alone.

definition: Social-representational and socio-institutional traditions concerned with shared meanings, collective representations, identities, norms and institutional contexts of educational life.
representative_cited_authors: F. Carugati (57); J. C. Turner (50); J. Xu (42); M. Dresel (42); C. Darnon (38); R. M. Baron (36); F. Butera (33); R. Rosenthal (32)
interpretive_use: Connects EJPE articles to a specifically European socio-institutional tradition in which education is studied through collective meaning and social context.

definition: Vygotskian, sociocultural, dialogic and activity-theoretical sources focused on mediation, language, tools, participation, collaboration, classroom discourse and culturally organised activity.
representative_cited_authors: L. S. Vygotsky (146); K. Aunola (71); B. Rogoff (69); R. Saljo (65); J. S. Bruner (61); E. Skinner (52); N. Mercer (51); S. Jarvela (47)
interpretive_use: Identifies one of the strongest continuities with the journal's historical focus on socially mediated learning and classroom interaction.

definition: Theoretical, philosophical, historical and reflexive sources used to clarify concepts, critique assumptions, reconstruct traditions or situate educational psychology within broader intellectual debates.
interpretive_use: Shows where citation ancestry contributes to conceptual reflection and historical self-understanding rather than only empirical modelling.
